The present invention addresses the problem of providing: a stainless steel which is provided with gas corrosion resistance suitable for substrates of compound thin film solar cells without requiring a surface treatment such as coating or plating; a method for producing this stainless steel; and a compound thin film solar cell which uses this stainless steel as a substrate. In order to solve the above-described problem, the present invention is characterized by forming an Fe—Cr—Al oxide film which has a film thickness of 15 nm or less and contains, in mass %, 0.03% or less of C, 2% or less of Si, 2% or less of Mn, 10-25% of Cr, 0.05% or less of P, 0.01% or less of S, 0.03% or less of N and 0.5-5% of Al, with the balance made up of Fe and unavoidable impurities, and wherein the maximum value of the Al concentration is 30% by mass or more and the Fe concentration at the depth of 2 nm from the surface is 30% or less in the profile of cation fractions excluding O and C ions. In addition, it is preferable that the surface film contains Si and Ti, while satisfying: Si is 0.3% or more; Ti is 0.03-0.5%; and (Mg+Ga) >0.001%. The surface film is obtained by carrying out annealing within the temperature range of 700-1,100° C. in a low-dew-point hydrogen gas.

The invention concerns the provision of a stainless steel that has gas-corrosion resistance appropriate for use as a substrate in compound thin-film solar cells, while eliminating the need for surface treatments such as coating or plating. It also relates to a manufacturing process for the stainless steel and to a compound thin-film solar cell employing the stainless steel as its substrate.

To achieve this, an Fe—Cr—Al oxide layer is formed with a thickness of 15 nm or less. The stainless steel contains, by mass, 0.03% or less C, 2% or less Si, 2% or less Mn, 10–25% Cr, 0.05% or less P, 0.01% or less S, 0.03% or less N, and 0.5–5% Al, with the remainder consisting of Fe and unavoidable impurities. In the cation-fraction depth profile, excluding O and C ions, the peak Al concentration is 30 mass% or higher, and the Fe concentration at a depth of 2 nm from the surface is 30% or lower.

It is also desirable for the surface film to include Si and Ti, with Si present at 0.3% or more, Ti present in an amount of 0.03–0.5%, and the combined amount of Mg and Ga satisfying the condition (Mg+Ga) > 0.001%. This surface film is produced by annealing the steel at 700–1,100° C. in hydrogen gas having a low dew point.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a stainless steel substrate suitable for use in compound thin film solar cells, particularly where high resistance to gas corrosion is required. The substrate achieves this corrosion resistance without the need for any additional surface treatment such as coating, plating, or deposition of a separate protective layer. As a result, the material can simplify the manufacturing process, reduce production cost, and avoid problems associated with adhesion or durability of external coatings.

The stainless steel substrate includes, on its surface, an Fe—Cr—Al-based oxide film having a thickness of 15 nm or less. The stainless steel itself contains controlled amounts of alloying elements and impurities. In particular, the composition is regulated with respect to carbon (C), silicon (Si), manganese (Mn), chromium (Cr), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), nitrogen (N), aluminum (Al), iron (Fe), and unavoidable impurities. By carefully limiting these components, the substrate can form a stable and highly protective oxide film while maintaining the mechanical and processing properties required for solar cell production.

The oxide film has a specific compositional profile that contributes to its gas corrosion resistance. The maximum aluminum concentration in the oxide film is at least 30% by mass, indicating that the film is enriched with aluminum oxide components that provide strong protective properties. In addition, the iron concentration at a depth of 2 nm from the outermost surface is 30% by mass or less. Suppressing iron near the surface is important because iron-rich oxides are generally less stable and more susceptible to corrosion under reactive gas environments. The combination of a high aluminum concentration and a controlled low iron concentration enables the formation of a dense, stable surface film that protects the stainless steel substrate.

In preferred embodiments, the surface oxide film further contains one or more additional elements, including silicon (Si), titanium (Ti), magnesium (Mg), and gallium (Ga), within specified concentration ranges. These elements can contribute to improving the stability, density, and corrosion resistance of the surface film. Their controlled incorporation may also improve compatibility with subsequent solar cell layers and enhance the durability of the substrate during high-temperature or reactive-gas processing.

The surface film is produced by annealing the stainless steel at a temperature of 700 to 1,100° C. in a hydrogen gas atmosphere having a low dew point. This heat treatment promotes selective oxidation and enrichment of aluminum at the surface, while limiting the formation of undesirable iron-rich oxides. The low-dew-point hydrogen atmosphere provides a controlled reducing environment that enables formation of a thin, uniform Fe—Cr—Al oxide film with the desired thickness and elemental distribution.

Through this combination of controlled stainless steel composition, a thin Fe—Cr—Al oxide surface film, high aluminum enrichment, suppressed near-surface iron concentration, and specialized annealing conditions, the invention provides a stainless steel substrate that is highly suitable for compound thin film solar cells and that exhibits excellent gas corrosion resistance without requiring coating or plating.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a stainless steel substrate suitable for use in compound thin film solar cells, particularly solar cells in which a compound semiconductor light-absorbing layer is formed on a metal substrate. In such solar cells, the substrate is required not only to have sufficient mechanical strength, heat resistance, and dimensional stability during high-temperature film formation, but also to exhibit resistance to corrosive gases that may be generated or used during the manufacturing process. Conventional stainless steel substrates may require additional surface treatments such as coating, plating, or the formation of a separate barrier layer in order to obtain adequate gas corrosion resistance. These additional steps can increase manufacturing cost, complicate production, and introduce problems such as poor adhesion, defects, or non-uniformity.

The present invention addresses these issues by providing a stainless steel material that inherently develops a protective surface film suitable for use in compound thin film solar cells. The stainless steel contains iron, chromium, and aluminum in controlled proportions, and is subjected to annealing under carefully selected conditions. In particular, the steel is annealed in hydrogen gas having a low dew point. By controlling the composition of the stainless steel and the atmosphere used during annealing, an extremely thin oxide film containing Fe, Cr, and Al is formed on the surface of the substrate.

This oxide film is not a separately applied coating or plated layer, but is generated from the stainless steel itself during the annealing process. As a result, the film is uniform, adherent, and compatible with the underlying metal substrate. The presence of chromium and aluminum in the oxide film contributes to improved resistance against corrosive gases, while the thinness of the film helps maintain the surface characteristics needed for subsequent formation of the solar-cell layers. Because the protective film is ultra-thin, it does not significantly interfere with the function of the substrate or with the deposition of the compound semiconductor layers.

The stainless steel substrate produced in this manner therefore provides excellent gas corrosion resistance without requiring additional coating or plating processes. This makes it particularly advantageous as a substrate for compound thin film solar cells, where exposure to corrosive atmospheres can occur during production or operation. The invention also simplifies the overall manufacturing process by eliminating separate surface-treatment steps, reducing cost, and improving productivity.

Accordingly, the invention provides a practical and efficient stainless steel substrate for compound thin film solar cells. By combining a specific Fe—Cr—Al stainless steel composition with annealing in a low-dew-point hydrogen atmosphere, the substrate forms a controlled protective oxide film on its surface. This structure enables the stainless steel to function effectively as a corrosion-resistant solar-cell substrate while maintaining ease of manufacture and suitability for large-scale production.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps us refer to something specific. For example, when we say “the book,” we are not talking about any book—we are talking about a particular book that the speaker and listener understand.

This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It can point to a known person, place, object, or idea, such as “the sun,” “the teacher,” or “the answer.” Without “the,” many sentences would feel incomplete or less precise.

Although “the” is easy to overlook, it is essential in everyday speech and writing. It helps organize meaning, connect ideas, and make language more exact. In this way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.output: A stainless steel substrate for a compound thin film solar cell is provided, the substrate having high heat resistance, corrosion resistance, and suitability for formation of a chalcopyrite or related compound semiconductor absorber layer. The substrate comprises, in mass percent, Cr: 10.5 to 35%, Ni: 0 to 25%, Mo: 0 to 6%, Mn: 0 to 5%, Si: 0.05 to 3%, Al: 0 to 3%, Ti and/or Nb: 0 to 1%, C: not more than 0.08%, N: not more than 0.10%, with the balance being Fe and unavoidable impurities. At least one surface of the substrate is provided with a controlled oxide film containing chromium oxide and/or silicon oxide and having a thickness of 5 to 200 nm, preferably 10 to 80 nm, whereby diffusion of Fe into an overlying electrode or compound semiconductor layer is suppressed. The substrate exhibits corrosion resistance such that no substantial pitting or red rust is produced after exposure to a chloride-containing aqueous solution or an acidic selenization/sulfurization atmosphere used in solar-cell manufacture. The substrate is annealed before or after oxide-film formation at 700 to 1,150°C in an inert, reducing, or controlled oxidizing atmosphere, and may further be subjected to a solar-cell process anneal at 400 to 650°C for 1 to 120 minutes during formation of a Cu—In—Ga—Se, Cu—Zn—Sn—S/Se, or other compound thin film. The resulting substrate maintains dimensional stability, adhesion, and barrier properties during high-temperature processing, thereby enabling manufacture of flexible or lightweight compound thin film solar cells having improved durability and conversion efficiency.

**Abstract**

Provided is a stainless steel sheet having excellent gas corrosion resistance, suitable for use as a substrate for compound thin film solar cells, without requiring any coating, plating, or other surface treatment. The stainless steel contains, in mass %, Cr in an amount sufficient to form a protective oxide film, and optionally one or more of Al, Si, Ti, Nb, Mo, and rare earth elements, with the balance being Fe and unavoidable impurities. counterfactuals.prompt: Produce an invention summary for a compound thin film solar cell substrate made of stainless steel, mentioning C, Si, Mn, Cr, P, S, N, Al composition limits, cation fraction depth profile, optional Si/Ti/Mg/Ga, and annealing conditions.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Summary

The invention relates to a stainless-steel substrate suitable for use in a compound thin film solar cell, such as a chalcopyrite-type solar cell including a CIGS, CIS, CZTS, or related compound semiconductor absorber layer. The substrate is designed to provide high heat resistance during absorber formation, good adhesion to back-electrode and semiconductor layers, and suppression of undesirable diffusion of Fe and other metal elements into the photoelectric conversion layer.

The substrate comprises a stainless-steel sheet having controlled alloy composition, in mass percent:

- C: not more than 0.03%
- Si: not more than 1.0%
- Mn: not more than 1.0%
- Cr: 10.5–30.0%
- P: not more than 0.05%
- S: not more than 0.03%
- N: not more than 0.05%
- Al: not more than 0.20%

with the balance being Fe and unavoidable impurities. In some embodiments, the stainless steel may be ferritic stainless steel, austenitic stainless steel, or a heat-resistant stainless steel optimized for thin film solar cell processing.

The surface of the stainless-steel substrate includes an oxide or modified surface layer formed by controlled annealing. In this surface layer, the cation fraction has a defined depth profile in which Cr is enriched near the surface relative to Fe, thereby forming a stable chromium-containing oxide that functions as a diffusion barrier. The Fe cation fraction is preferably lower at the outermost surface and increases toward the interior of the steel, while the Cr cation fraction is higher at or near the surface and decreases with depth. This graded cation profile improves barrier performance and adhesion without requiring a thick separately deposited insulating layer.

The substrate may optionally contain or be surface-modified with one or more of Si, Ti, Mg, and Ga. These elements may be present in the stainless steel composition, in a surface oxide layer, or in a separate interfacial layer. They can improve oxidation behavior, enhance insulating properties, reduce diffusion of Fe and Cr into the absorber layer, and improve adhesion of a molybdenum back contact or other electrode layer. In particular, Si, Ti, Mg, or Ga may form oxides or mixed oxides distributed in the surface region, contributing to a stable cation fraction depth profile.

The surface-modified stainless-steel substrate is produced by annealing the steel sheet under controlled conditions. The annealing may be performed in an oxidizing, weakly oxidizing, inert, reducing, or controlled dew-point atmosphere at a temperature sufficient to form the desired chromium-rich surface oxide layer. Typical annealing conditions include a temperature of about 600–1,100°C for several seconds to several hours, depending on sheet thickness and atmosphere. In one embodiment, annealing is carried out at 700–950°C in an atmosphere having controlled oxygen potential or water vapor content so that selective oxidation of Cr, and optionally Si, Ti, Mg, or Ga, occurs near the surface.

After annealing, a back electrode layer, such as Mo, may be formed directly or indirectly on the stainless-steel substrate, followed by deposition of a compound semiconductor absorber layer, buffer layer, transparent conductive layer, and other solar cell layers. The resulting substrate suppresses metal contamination of the absorber, withstands high-temperature processing, and provides improved conversion efficiency and long-term reliability for compound thin film solar cells.
